Manual verification
- Part 2 page 1037, Part 3 page 43, Part 6 page 70 and Part 4 page 322: the parsed text itself remains in legacy/Zawgyi glyph order for whole passages (the dependent e-vowel appears before its base in the output order). These are real page-level parsing/conversion failures, not only 2-3 isolated words.
- Part 3 page 43 also retains stray Latin glyphs inside Burmese words, e.g. A/U/semicolon substitutions in the parsed text.
- Part 1 page 2 is mixed: "နှင့်/နှင့်ဆေးလိပ်" is correctly spelled in the output but its coda mark is emitted as {F}; the following title begins with legacy e-order and is a real order issue.
- Part 1 page 20 and Part 8 page 7 are readable Unicode pages. Their sampled {F} hits are mainly the Burmese comma and syllable-coda fragments from correctly spelled words.

Verdict
- YES: the fresh Parser output contains real broken pages. The severe cases are whole-page/passages left in glyph order, plus occasional stray Latin glyphs.
- NO: {F} count must not be read as a broken-word count. Most {F} forms are single dependent marks or punctuation produced by POS segmentation, including on correctly spelled Unicode pages.
- Against the 2-3/page negligible rule: isolated impossible/stray sequences are low overall (impossible 0.16/page, stray 0.18/page), but the glyph-order pages exceed negligence by page/passages, not by a few words.
